report.headline: Forecast as of 2006-12-02 finds ILLUMINATE (torcetrapib) not computable due to insufficient data, with HDL-C non-causality and uncertain CETP genetics as fundamental concerns.
report.summary: The calculator returns not_computable for ILLUMINATE (NCT00134264), a 15,067-patient trial testing torcetrapib 60 mg QD plus atorvastatin versus atorvastatin alone on time to first major cardiovascular event. The primary category is insufficient_data: no placebo-adjusted LDL-C or apoB data exist at the phase 3 dose pre-cutoff, follow-up duration and event count are unknown, and power cannot be computed. The calculator estimates an expected HR of 0.838 (16.2% RRR) based on a -26% apoB reduction from phase 1 at 120 mg BID (not placebo-adjusted, wrong dose, 14 days only), requiring ~1,003 events for 80% power. Two secondary categories are supported: biomarker_not_causal (HDL-C classified as non-causal in the reference table; torcetrapib was developed to raise HDL-C, with phase 2 showing 40.2% HDL-C increase at 90 mg/day) and target_not_causal (Open Targets CETP genetic association score 0.736 but evidence_before_cutoff = 0; calculator identifies 'target genetics: uncertain' as weakest link). LDL-C data at 60 mg are contradictory (-22.2% and +0.1%, both not placebo-adjusted). Confidence is medium.

Phase 2 placebo-adjusted HDL-C increase 40.2% at 90 mg/day (closest to phase 3 60 mg QD) (Efficacy and safety of torcetrapib, a novel cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibitor, in individuals with below-average high-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels on a background of atorvastatin.)

Phase 1 apoB reduction -26% at 120 mg BID (not placebo-adjusted, wrong dose vs phase 3 60 mg QD, 14 days only) (Raising high-density lipoprotein in humans through inhibition of cholesteryl ester transfer protein: an initial multidose study of torcetrapib.)

Contradictory LDL-C at 60 mg: -22.2% and +0.1%, both not placebo-adjusted, same PMID (Efficacy and safety of torcetrapib, a novel cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibitor, in individuals with below-average high-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels.)
Primary endpoint: time to first occurrence of a major cardiovascular disease event (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00134264 ILLUMINATE)
Calculator assumptions: apoB baseline assumed 80 mg/dL; follow-up unknown, effect shown at 5 years; events needed for 80% power: 1,003 (calculator)
report.what_would_change_this: Phase 3 dose-specific (60 mg QD) placebo-adjusted LDL-C and apoB changes; actual trial follow-up duration and event count; pre-cutoff human genetic studies linking CETP variants to coronary disease outcomes.
report.readthrough_note: Other CETP inhibitor programmes (dalcetrapib, anacetrapib, evacetrapib) were in development around this time; the same HDL-C non-causality concern would apply to any agent whose primary intended biomarker is HDL-C elevation.

mechanism.notes: HDL-C input uses placebo-adjusted 40.2% at 90 mg/day (f_75056971f04153), closest available dose to phase 3 60 mg QD. LDL-C has no placebo-adjusted data; within-arm phase 2 values at 60 mg contradict (-22.2% vs +0.1%, same PMID), so LDL-C change set to null. apoB input uses within-arm -26% at 120 mg BID phase 1 (f_4b7d1014c711ee), not placebo-adjusted, wrong dose/phase; no placebo-adjusted apoB at 60 mg QD exists pre-cutoff. Genetic evidence all post-cutoff, target_genetics uncertain. Trial event-driven, follow-up and event count unknown at cut-off.

for.text: HDL-C is classified as non-causal in the reference table; torcetrapib was developed specifically to raise HDL-C.
Phase 2 placebo-adjusted data at 90 mg/day (closest to phase 3 60 mg QD) shows 40.2% HDL-C increase at 8 weeks.
Higher doses show even larger HDL-C increases (136% at 120 mg QD, 91% at 120 mg BID), confirming potent on-target biomarker effect.

hypotheses.would_settle: Post-cutoff Mendelian randomization studies confirming HDL-C non-causality for coronary disease.

for.text: Open Targets genetic association score for CETP is 0.736 but evidence_before_cutoff = 0 (all 13 studies published after 2006-12-02).
Calculator identifies 'target genetics: uncertain' as weakest_link; for a well-studied target like CETP, absence of pre-cutoff genetic evidence means target causality cannot be established.

hypotheses.would_settle: Pre-cutoff human genetic studies linking CETP variants to coronary disease outcomes.

for.text: Calculator estimates expected HR 0.838 (16.2% RRR) based on apoB -26% reduction, requiring ~1,003 events for 80% power.

against.text: apoB -26% comes from phase 1 at 120 mg BID (not placebo-adjusted, wrong dose vs phase 3 60 mg QD, wrong phase, 14 days only).
LDL-C data at 60 mg is contradictory: within-arm -22.2% (f_283f459bc7bd59) vs +0.1% (f_60e8aed5c71108), both not placebo-adjusted, same PMID.
No placebo-adjusted LDL-C or apoB data at the phase 3 dose (60 mg QD) exists pre-cutoff; follow-up duration and event count unknown, so power cannot be computed.

hypotheses.would_settle: Phase 3 dose-specific (60 mg QD) placebo-adjusted LDL-C and apoB changes; actual trial follow-up and event count.

against.text: No blood pressure, aldosterone, or cardiovascular safety data from phase 1/2 trials appear in the verified facts as of the 2006-12-02 cutoff.

hypotheses.would_settle: Pre-cutoff phase 1/2 safety data on BP, electrolytes, aldosterone, and adverse events.

against.text: Trial enrolls high-risk patients (CHD or risk equivalents) but no evidence in verified facts that this population is mismatched to CETP inhibition mechanism.

hypotheses.would_settle: Subgroup analyses by baseline risk or lipid levels; genetic evidence of CETP effect modification by population.

against.text: Primary endpoint is time to first major CVD event (standard composite); no follow-up duration reported in verified facts to assess if too short.

hypotheses.would_settle: Planned follow-up duration and event accrual rate from protocol.

against.text: No data on recruitment, adherence, or sponsor decisions in verified facts as of cutoff.

hypotheses.would_settle: Trial conduct metrics, DSMB minutes, sponsor communications.

issues.issue: off_target_harm hypothesis references non-existent facts f_0b6d4eea72218e and f_52a060d63dbeee (not in verified facts list). The 'for' and 'against' sections have empty refs arrays. Every claim must cite verified facts.
issues.request: Remove references to non-existent facts. Populate 'for' and 'against' with actual verified facts, or mark as 'no pre-cutoff safety data available' with empty refs explicitly noted.

issues.issue: Multiple hypotheses have empty refs arrays in 'against' sections: population, design_or_endpoint, off_target_harm. The 'against' claims (e.g., 'CETP inhibition mechanism should be relevant', 'no design flaw evident', 'no BP/aldosterone data in verified facts') need supporting references or must be removed.
issues.request: Add verified fact references to all 'against' claims, or remove unsupported claims. For 'no data available' statements, cite the absence explicitly (e.g., 'no BP data in verified facts as of cutoff').

issues.issue: LDL-C change used by calculator (-22.2%, f_283f459bc7bd59) is within-arm, not placebo-adjusted, AND directly contradicted by f_60e8aed5c71108 (+0.1% at same dose/adjustment from same PMID). The calculator basis 'LDL-C' and expected_hr 0.896 rely on this unreliable input.
issues.request: Re-evaluate LDL-C input: either (a) use placebo-adjusted LDL-C if available at 60 mg, (b) note the contradiction explicitly in calculator assumptions, or (c) set LDL-C change to null given the conflict. The current input overstates evidence for LDL-C lowering.

issues.issue: apoB change (-26%, f_4b7d1014c711ee) is from phase 1 at 120 mg BID (not placebo-adjusted), not the phase 3 dose of 60 mg QD. Verified facts show phase 2 apoB data at 120 mg QD and 120 mg BID (f_43f1805755dcf3, f_4a08f698b34a3b, f_5e72aa9582a243) but all are within-arm and at wrong dose. No placebo-adjusted apoB at 60 mg QD exists pre-cutoff.
issues.request: Either remove apoB from calculator inputs (since no relevant dose/placebo-adjusted data exists) or add explicit caveat that apoB input is from wrong dose/phase and not placebo-adjusted. Current method field notes this but input is still used.

issues.issue: HDL-C change (54.5%, f_6551c771a27ddb) is placebo-adjusted but dose is 'not stated'. Phase 3 dose is 60 mg QD. Verified facts show HDL-C 40.2% at 90 mg/day (f_75056971f04153) and 136% at 120 mg QD (f_8c0a2c11451cd5). The 54.5% likely reflects a higher dose. This overstates expected HDL-C effect at the trial dose.
issues.request: Use the dose-specific placebo-adjusted HDL-C change closest to 60 mg QD. f_75056971f04153 (40.2% at 90 mg/day) is closer than unstated dose. Update calculator input and hypothesis references accordingly.

issues.issue: Target genetics set to 'uncertain' with Open Targets score 0.736 but evidence_before_cutoff=0. Prior critic feedback suggested 'not_causal' or 'uncertain'. While 'uncertain' is defensible, the rationale should explicitly address: CETP is well-studied, zero pre-cutoff coronary-disease genetic evidence, high post-cutoff score. This affects weakest_link interpretation.
issues.request: Add explicit rationale in calculator assumptions or hypothesis 'target_not_causal' for why 'uncertain' was chosen over 'not_causal' given zero pre-cutoff evidence for a well-studied target.

issues.issue: Calculator assumptions state 'LDL-C: no baseline given, assumed 2.0' but the LDL-C input itself is contradictory and within-arm. The expected_hr 0.896 and causal_rrr 0.104 are presented as precise estimates despite unreliable input. The 'insufficient_data' category is correct but the point estimate may mislead.
issues.request: Add assumption caveat: 'LDL-C change based on within-arm phase 2 data contradicted by same source; expected HR highly uncertain.' Consider whether to suppress point estimate when basis biomarker is unreliable.

issues.issue: off_target_harm hypothesis contains an 'against' claim with zero fact references: 'No blood pressure, aldosterone, or cardiovascular safety data from phase 1/2 trials appear in the verified facts as of the 2006-12-02 cutoff.' All claims must cite verified fact IDs; an argument from absence in the store is not a citable fact. Either add a fact confirming no pre-cutoff safety data was published, or remove the unsupported 'against' entry.
issues.request: Remove or fix the unsupported 'against' claim in off_target_harm hypothesis; every claim requires a verified fact reference.

issues.issue: execution_or_nonscientific hypothesis contains an 'against' claim with zero fact references: 'No data on recruitment, adherence, or sponsor decisions in verified facts as of cutoff.' Same violation: absence in the store is not a citable fact.
issues.request: Remove or fix the unsupported 'against' claim in execution_or_nonscientific hypothesis.

issues.issue: Calculator uses apoB -26% (f_4b7d1014c711ee) as the basis for expected_hr (0.838) despite this value being: (a) not placebo-adjusted (within-arm only), (b) from phase 1 at 120 mg BID (wrong dose vs phase 3 60 mg QD), (c) wrong phase (phase 1 vs phase 3), (d) short duration (14 days). The automatic check flagged this. With HDL-C non-causal and LDL-C contradictory/null, there is NO valid causal biomarker change at the phase 3 dose. The expected_hr should be 1.0 (null effect) or the basis should be 'none' with a clear caveat, not a precise 0.838 derived from invalid data.
issues.request: Re-run calculator with apoB excluded as a basis (since it fails placebo-adjustment, dose, phase, and duration criteria). Expected HR should reflect 'no valid causal biomarker data at phase 3 dose' -> expected_hr 1.0 or null, category 'insufficient_data'.

issues.issue: HDL-C input uses 40.2% at 90 mg/day (f_75056971f04153) as 'closest available dose to phase 3 60 mg QD'. While this is the best available placebo-adjusted value, the dose mismatch (90 mg vs 60 mg) is a caveat. The verified facts show no placebo-adjusted HDL-C at 60 mg QD. This is acceptable as a forecast input per instructions (missing phase 3 biomarker data is a caveat, never a reason to drop a quantified verified input), but should be explicitly noted in calculator assumptions.
issues.request: Add calculator assumption: 'HDL-C 40.2% from 90 mg/day (not 60 mg QD phase 3 dose); dose-response uncertainty.'

issues.issue: LDL-C data at 60 mg from the same PMID (17084249) shows contradictory within-arm values (-22.2% vs +0.1%), both not placebo-adjusted. This suggests either data extraction error or subgroup/analysis differences in the source. The calculator correctly sets LDL-C to null, but the contradiction should be flagged as a data quality concern for the mechanism analyst.
issues.request: Note in calculator assumptions: 'LDL-C at 60 mg: contradictory within-arm values in same source (pmid:17084249), neither placebo-adjusted; data quality uncertain.'

issues.issue: Calculator assumes apoB baseline 80 mg/dL ('apoB: no baseline given, assumed 80.0') without a verified fact. This assumption drives the ldl_equivalent_mmol calculation (0.712) and expected_hr. Since apoB input is already invalid (see high-severity issue), this assumption compounds the error.
issues.request: Remove apoB baseline assumption once apoB is excluded as basis; if any apoB analysis is retained, source a verified fact for baseline apoB in this population.

issues.issue: Target genetics set to 'uncertain' with Open Targets score 0.736 but evidence_before_cutoff=0. Prior critic feedback suggested 'not_causal' or 'uncertain' for well-studied target with zero pre-cutoff evidence. 'Uncertain' is defensible but the rationale should be explicit in calculator assumptions.
issues.request: Add calculator assumption: 'CETP target genetics: Open Targets score 0.736 but 0 pre-cutoff studies; set to uncertain per rule for well-studied target with no pre-cutoff evidence.'
